_comment: person_id-bounded slicing plan for the ulslo-deploy toFHIR job (ai4hf-dis critical path). toFHIR accumulates its whole mapped result set before writing (FhirMappingJobManager.scala:762, ErroneousRecordWriter.scala:94) - there is no streaming/foreachBatch path, so Spark JDBC partitioning does NOT bound memory. The only lever is SqlSource.query with an explicit row-range predicate. Slices are person-ORDINAL ranges (row_number() over person_id order), never raw person_id literals, so the plan never encodes patient-identifying values.
_sizing_method: Measured 2026-09-10 via .github/diag/ai4hf_dis_slice_distribution.sql (uls-lisboa-ocidental/teras-cluster-uls-lisboa-ocidental) against 200-person ordinal buckets, run 34442391625. Linear fit of RSS(Mi) = 425 + 0.0412 * rows from the two established RSS/rowcount points (20776 rows -> 1281Mi, 102921 rows -> 4664Mi). Target ceiling 4500Mi (below the demonstrated-safe 4664Mi point) => ~98.9K rows/slice-execution. Applied a further 10% margin against extrapolation error since bucket widths below are scaled, not independently measured => target ~89-95K rows/slice. bucket_width_persons per mapping = 200 * (target_rows / measured_max_rows_at_200), rounded down to a clean number.

cause-of-death-mapping.reason: death table is 3793 rows total, well under any per-slice ceiling

_caveat: worst_slice_est_rows extrapolates linearly from the 200-person-bucket measurement; it is NOT independently measured at the listed bucket_width_persons. TASK 5 (green proof) must confirm at least the largest mapping's largest slice against this estimate before the plan is trusted at scale.
